items.headline: Jet fuel raised ₹1.37 a litre to ₹138.50, a fourth monthly rise; commercial LPG up ₹10 to ₹2,820
items.summary: Household LPG held at ₹942 per cylinder. Second straight monthly hike in commercial LPG as international benchmarks firm. Ongoing pass-through of high oil.
items.rationale: Dearer jet fuel squeezes airline margins and fares; commercial LPG adds to restaurant and small-business costs, while frozen household prices keep the subsidy burden on the state.

items.headline: Iran says talks are under way on a two-day plan to reopen Hormuz; envoys meet Qatari and Pakistani mediators
items.summary: Tehran wants sanctions lifted, oil waivers restored and frozen funds released; another official called Qatar's ideas unacceptable. Iran's leader ordered an 'unrestricted response' to any attack. Diplomacy advancing but contested.
items.rationale: A quick reopening would sharply lower India's oil, LNG and freight costs; failure raises the risk of US strikes after the 3 November vote.

items.headline: Foreign investors pulled ₹52,100 crore from Indian equities in October; 2026 outflows reach ₹3.12 lakh crore
items.summary: Up from ₹48,056 crore reported mid-month despite late-month buying. Crude near $114, US yields and the pull of AI stocks elsewhere drove selling. Foreign funds also sold debt. Ongoing.
items.rationale: Persistent foreign selling weighs on large caps and the rupee, leaving domestic funds to absorb supply.

items.headline: Rupee ends October with its best month since February, up about 0.6–1%
items.summary: RBI steps included a special oil-dollar window and moving oil-related dollar buying off the spot market, while tight liquidity made shorting the rupee costly. Reversing earlier weakness.
items.rationale: A steadier rupee eases imported inflation and reassures foreign investors, but relies on RBI support as reserves fall.

items.headline: India's record crude imports point to strong refinery runs; Russian oil buying to stay flexible
items.summary: Refiners keep buying heavily despite prices near $118, shifting between Gulf and Russian grades on price. Continues last week's sourcing shift.
items.rationale: High refinery runs support fuel exports and refining margins, but record volumes at high prices swell the import bill.

items.headline: US Navy could escort ships through Hormuz with an international coalition, Treasury Secretary says
items.summary: Comes as October set a record for ship attacks and Iran claims tankers on unauthorised routes caught fire. New proposal.
items.rationale: Escorts could restore some tanker traffic and ease freight and insurance costs for India, but risk direct clashes.

items.headline: India and Turkey propose ideas to resume Black Sea grain shipments, US says at G20
items.summary: Black Sea attacks have made it deadlier than Hormuz; Türkiye submitted proposals to the US and others call for a truce. Builds on last week's corridor proposal.
items.rationale: Restored Black Sea flows would ease world grain and edible oil prices, helping India's food inflation.

items.headline: At G20, India flags Hormuz ship attacks and urges shielding energy markets from sanctions and chokepoints
items.summary: The external affairs minister said the Global South bears the burden and Indian seafarers face risks. Follows attacks on ships with Indian crews. Diplomatic push.
items.rationale: Signals India's push for supply security; limited direct market effect but supports diplomacy that could lower energy risk.
